I have 8 mu of land. My husband works in the county town part of the year, but I'm the one who decides what to plant — I've been farming since I was a little girl, even though I'm only 37 now. I never went to school, can't read or write, but I know my fields. I watch what my neighbors do, and I do what worked last year.

Last year my wheat on 6.5 mu gave me about 1000 jin per mu. That was alright. I use lumai seeds, same as the family across the road — they're reliable and I can get them from the shop in town. In early October I'll rotary till that land and sow the wheat. I put down about two big bags of ammonium bicarbonate per mu before planting, and then I topdress two more times when the wheat turns green in spring. I can't afford more than that — fertilizer prices keep going up and I need to keep some cash for my children's school fees. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help the wheat settle, and twice in spring when the rain doesn't come. The pump electricity is expensive so I don't water more than that. I spray about seven times for wheat — herbicide once at the start, bug spray three times when I see aphids, and fungicide twice because two years ago the yellow rust came and I lost yield. I don't want that again.

After wheat harvest around June 6th, I have maybe four or five days before I must plant maize. There is no time to till the land — I plant denghai 605 hybrid seeds directly, no-tillage. One package per mu from the seed dealer. I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu total for the maize. I irrigate twice if the rain is bad in July and August. Four sprays — herbicide once and insecticide three times when the corn borers show up.

On the other 1.5 mu I grow cotton with mungbean between the rows. I rotary till that plot in mid-April. Cotton gives good cash but the bollworms are terrible every year — last year I sprayed 16 times, almost every week in the hot months. I use guoxinmian 3 seeds. The mungbean doesn't need much, just one watering and two sprays. It comes off in July and then the cotton keeps growing until October.

I do what my neighbors do. If the families who do well use lumai wheat and denghai maize, so do I. I don't try new seeds or new methods because if they fail, my family doesn't eat. Last year was fine. The weather looks normal this year. So I will do the same.
